- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is over-optimistic, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7) and forecast shows strong mean reversion, delay correction until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just historical mean.  
- When sentiment is consistently low and price is falling, avoid forecasting sharp rebounds — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent low for 5 days.  
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 days to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” traps.
